C0.quote: to improve the robustness of LLM ranking queries
C0.note: Applies Partial Borda voting to aggregate repeated LLM rankings (LLM answers play the role of voters); borderline but a voting rule is the main tool.

C1.quote: Our experiments show that our approach significantly improves the robustness
C1.note: Experiments use ChatGPT-generated queries and answers, treated as synthetic; AX from Prop 4.4 and reinterpreted properties.

C2.2.quote: We will therefore focus on preferences expressed by partial orderings.
C2.2.note: Partial orders over outcomes (top-ranked answers preferred to non-mentioned, which are incomparable).

C2.3.quote: captures the preferences expressed by them.
C2.3.note: Preferences are described as expressed; in the application the inputs are LLM answers, no separate held attitude.

C2.4.quote: captures the preferences expressed by them.
C2.4.note: Input described as expressed rankings only.

C5.1.note: Evaluation is by robustness (Kendall, Spearman correlations), not welfare-type criteria.

VOT.quote_behav: instead of asking a query once, we ask it repeatedly
VOT.note: Voters are repeated LLM answers, fixed by the sampling procedure; no strategic behaviour.

ORG.note: Authors' pipeline, not an agent in the model.
